// Every line here is one identifier away from a line in the fixture that breaks
// the rules, and every one of them is legal in any layer.

package kernel

import (
	"fmt"
	"math"
	"strings"
)

// Formatting is not printing. A returned error and a built string are how a
// layer below the command line says something.
func describe(total float64) (string, error) {
	var b strings.Builder
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "the total is %v", total)
	if total < 0 {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("the total is %v, which is not a level", total)
	}
	return fmt.Sprintf("%s\n", b.String()), nil
}

// Arithmetic that is not a logarithm or an exponential. Every one of these is a
// function of the same package and none of them is decibel arithmetic.
func geometry(area, length float64) float64 {
	return math.Sqrt(area) + math.Abs(length) + math.Max(area, length) + math.Round(area)
}

// An identifier that happens to be spelled like one of the rules is not one.
type math2 struct{ Log float64 }

func (m math2) value() float64 { return m.Log }
